relations.subject: xdcr:replication
relations.evidence: Once a replication has been deleted, you may also wish to delete the _reference_ on which it was based. See [Delete a Reference](delete-xdcr-reference.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page is almost entirely a thin click-through/CLI/REST procedure (delete, confirm, done) with no new access-control or structural fact of its own. It does not restate create-xdcr-reference.json's own constraint that a reference cannot be deleted while a replication depends on it - the constraint appears only on the reference side, never as a mirrored statement here on the replication side ('you must delete replications before the reference', for example, is implied by the Next Steps ordering but never asserted in prose).

cross_component_finding: This page's REST example ('If the call is successful, no output is displayed') is a small but real contrast with delete-xdcr-reference.md's own REST example (this same batch), which DOES return a body (`"ok"`) on success - two sibling delete endpoints in the same feature area with different, undocumented response-body conventions. Not modeled as a relation since no page states the asymmetry is deliberate; recorded here as a documentation-consistency observation.
